correctness.rationale: For each vertical center, centering horizontal slices uniquely maximizes the two-interval overlap. Direct integration gives A_t(y)=4y-6(1-t)y^2 for y<=1/2 and A_t(y)=4t(1-y)+2(1-t)(1-y)^2 for y>=1/2. The second branch is strictly decreasing; the first has vertex y=1/[3(1-t)], feasible exactly through t=1/3. Division by area 1+t yields both formulas. Monotonicity, one-sided second derivatives (81/32,-27/32) and sharp square-root endpoint follow by elementary symbolic algebra. An independent rational polygon-clipping checker and symbolic verification both passed. The checker alone is not a universal proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural affine-invariant exact profile for all genuine trapezoids gives the largest centrally symmetric subset without per-instance optimization, identifies the only shape parameter that a point-symmetry ratio can recover, and determines a genuine optimizer transition at t=1/3. Exact inverse formulas and the sharp square-root breakdown at triangular degeneration explain limits of geometric identification. This is not a trivial substitution, arbitrary finite slice or mere numerical reproduction of a known table.
